Issued at 335 AM EDT Mon Aug 31 2026

Coverage of light showers has diminished as of 06Z as ridge of lower 
low-mid level theta-e air has advected into northeast IL/northwest 
IN. A ribbon of much higher low-mid level theta-e air is already 
rapidly advecting back across north central Illinois and is expected 
to nose into Lake Michigan vicinity, far NW IN, SW Lower MI 
through daybreak. Isentropic progs in the 310-315K layer do 
show a decent signal of stronger isentropic ascent closer to 12Z
across far northeast Illinois into southwest Lower Michigan 
eventually shifting across far northern IN/southern Lower 
MI/northwest OH this afternoon. Approach of this higher low 
level theta-e air today will finally mark an uptick in more 
respectable low level moisture transport into the local area 
along with the leading edge of some steeper mid level lapse 
rates. Along with this advection will come warmer mid level 
profiles that will likely make sfc based convection difficult to
come by locally. Nonetheless, did continue scattered PoPs today
to account for this more substantial advective push, although 
coverage remains an item of somewhat lower confidence with 
uncertainty in how warmer mid level profiles will affect shower 
potential. 

By mid afternoon into this evening, attention will turn to an upper 
level short wave which has ts origins from southwest CONUS as 
it continues northeast from the Central Plains. Isentropic progs
of the same 310-315k layer do show a quick increase in strength
of isentropic lift across northern Illinois mid-late afternoon 
shifting into northern IN late afternoon/evening. This secondary
round of forcing could result in another round of isolated-
scattered showers, particularly across the north. MUCAPEs over 
1000 J/kg are possible this afternoon, although there will 
likely be some CIN in a 100-mb mixed layer sense. Severe weather
is not expected today.

The main story for today will be the increased heat/humidity. 
Moisture advection today should result in increasing sfc dew points 
to the lower 70s. Mixing heights remain quite shallow today 
under the influence of the warm advection, but even mixing up 
to 900 mb would support highs in mid 80s to around 90. This 
combination of temps/dew points should push heat indices into 
the 90 to 95 range, although like yesterday will have to monitor
how convective trends/cloud cover impact hourly temps/heat 
indices.

The aformentioned Central Plains vort max should push across 
northern Indiana tonight with a continued potential of 
isolated/scattered showers in the evening in a zone of 
preceding isentropic ascent. Late tonight confidence wanes in 
shower potential as warmer mid level profiles become more
established. One interesting item to note in higher res 
guidance is development of convection late tonight across Corn 
Belt in right entrance region of Upper Midwest jet streak, and 
at the nose of weak to modest low level jet impinging on the 
strong 925-800 mb theta-e gradient. Some CAMS attempt to bring 
this convection across northeast IL into southern Lower MI 
toward midday Tuesday, but confidence in this scenario is very 
low given possibility that convection may remain more elevated 
and take a northward route. Some indications in guidance that a 
weak mid level trough (possibly convectively enhanced) could 
dampen the mid level heights/temps just a bit by Tuesday 
afternoon to cause some concern for isolated storms developing 
in what could be moderately to strongly buoyant environment. 
There should be some decent westerly deep layer shear across far
northern IN/southern Lower MI Tuesday afternoon (~30-35 knots).
Main item of uncertainty is a forcing mechanism on Tuesday, as 
the potential weak mid level trough could exit early in the 
afternoon with some subtle mid level height rises later in the 
day. Given this low confidence scenario have included some 
slight chance PoPs Tuesday across the north, with a potential of
an isolated strong to severe storm (wind/hail) due to 
background shear/instability.

For Wednesday, the stronger negative upper height anomaly across 
Ontario will shift into western Quebec helping to drive a cold 
frontal boundary across central Lower Michigan during the day. 
Instability/shear profiles could potentially support another day of 
at least an isolated severe risk, but a good deal of uncertainty 
exists again Wednesday dealing with the fact stronger mid/upper 
level forcing may be vacating the area late in the day, and some 
question as to existence of any weak to moderate surface based CIN 
into early evening.

An item of higher forecast confidence for Tuesday and Wednesday 
continues to be the potential of heat indices around the 100 degree 
mark for much of the area. Forecast thermal profiles support highs 
around 90 on Tuesday and in the low to potentially mid 90s
